newsitem.title: MONACO: Rainier urges Albert to marry as Monaco celebrates.
newsitem.headline: Rainier urges Albert to marry as Monaco celebrates.

text.p: Tiny Monaco launched a 10-month celebration of its 700th birthday on Wednesday as ageing Prince Rainier III urged his son Albert to find a bride.

In interviews on the eve of the festivities, Rainier, 73, said the 38-year-old Albert -- one of the most eligible bachelors in the world -- had more work to do before he could succeed him and perhaps would have to marry first.
"He must sharpen his skills...I think he must gain some experience before he is completely ready to take over," Rainier told French television TF 1.

In a separate interview with France 2, he hinted that marriage and a family were part of the preparations for a handover, which he said could "perhaps, probably" take place before the end of the century.
"There is also the question of his marriage," Rainier said. "I would like him to take things in hand and at the same time start a family."
The balding Albert, who has often been photographed with the likes of Claudia Schiffer, Brooke Shields and Lisa-Marie Presley, has previously hinted marriage was not a priority.
Asked this week if he would marry in the next few months, he told an interviewer: "No - you'll know soon enough."
Albert confirmed there was no precise date for a handover in an interview aired just hours before his family gathered at Monaco's cathedral on Wednesday to begin the celebrations.
"I do not know at all whether that will take place in the coming months, this year or in coming years. I cannot say at the moment," he told RMC Radio.

Several thousand local residents, tourists and other well-wishers gathered for the morning mass launching the celebration of the Grimaldi dynasty's 700th year in power over this lilliputian state with a population of just 30,000 and less than two square km (one square mile) of territory.
Rainier, the 29th Grimaldi to rule Monaco since 1297, was expected to make a speech later in the day.

More than $200 million has been set aside for celebrations, which are to last through October and include sporting events, car races, concerts, art shows, plays -- and a meeting of the International Whaling Commission to demonstrate the principality's marine and environmental dedication.
A sliver of choice Riviera real estate in the southeastern corner of France, Monaco is best known for what is officially referred to as "the princely family" headed by Rainier.
The much-photographed but star-crossed family has been in the public eye ever since Prince Rainier married American film star Grace Kelly in 1956.

Kelly died in a 1982 car crash but the rest of her family -- which also includes the striking Princesses Caroline, 39, and Stephanie, 31 -- has remained ever since on the glossy covers of photo magazines.
